responseText: {"title":"Lines Moving Outward","question":"When marks spread away from a figure, what do they carry with them?","introduction":"Seventeen works share a single structural habit: lines, waves, zigzags, or spikes move outward from a central form. But the mood that travels with those marks shifts constantly — from stillness to noise, from containment to release. This exhibition follows that spread across four chapters, asking what changes when the radiating mark is tight or loose, orderly or frantic, and when the center itself begins to dissolve.","closing":"Each work sends marks outward from something. Whether those marks feel like pressure, heat, noise, or escape depends on what the center looks like — and how much of it remains.","chapters":[{"title":"Still Centers, Spreading Lines","introduction":"Three works open the exhibition with the simplest version of the question: a single dark figure on a flat field, lines fanning outward in every direction with almost no competing marks.","stops":[{"slot":"W296","whyHere":"A seated black rabbit with X eyes sits motionless while yellow zigzag and wave lines spread outward in two distinct registers — tight jolts above, slower rolls to the sides. The stillness of the figure and the agitation of the surrounding lines establish the exhibition's core tension.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W261","whyHere":"A squat black form on yellow-green ground, red lines radiating outward. Like W296, the figure is inert and the lines are active, but the red-on-green field sharpens the contrast between body and surround.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works place a motionless black silhouette against a flat saturated field, but the color shift from red to acid green changes the temperature of the surrounding scatter."},{"slot":"W242","whyHere":"A black mass suspended by a single diagonal line, jagged zigzags spreading across unbroken yellow. The hanging posture introduces precariousness absent from the seated figures before it.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where the previous figures sit grounded on a horizon strip, this form hangs from a taut line, making the radiating marks feel less like heat and more like instability."}]},{"title":"The Figure Gains a Face","introduction":"Four works add facial features — eyes, mouths, spiral marks — to the radiating silhouette, asking whether a legible face changes how the surrounding lines read.","stops":[{"slot":"W240","whyHere":"A rounded black figure with a small disc face sits low in the frame; yellow lines spread outward against deep orange. The face is barely readable, keeping the image close to the previous chapter's silhouettes.","transitionFromPrevious":"The shift from hanging to seated restores groundedness, and the orange field warms the image, but the figure's minimal face marks a threshold between pure silhouette and readable presence."},{"slot":"W104","whyHere":"A black oval with spiral eyes and a serrated grin floats above a flat yellow field, wavy lines radiating outward and a coiling tether dropping to a small reaching hand. The face is now fully legible and the mood tips toward unease.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous figure's face was a faint disc; here spiral eyes and a toothed mouth make the center unmistakably expressive, and the radiating lines shift from neutral scatter to something more charged."},{"slot":"W101","whyHere":"A reclining animal form packed with yellow cross-hatching, red X eyes, yellow zigzags spreading across blue. The figure is no longer upright or floating — it reclines — and the interior is filled with marks rather than left as flat black.","transitionFromPrevious":"W104's figure was a clean black oval; here the body is dense with interior scribbling, so the radiating lines outside feel like an extension of internal restlessness rather than external pressure."},{"slot":"W128","whyHere":"A stick-limbed figure stands wide-legged, overlapping purple and gold discs spreading behind its upper body, a jagged yellow disc replacing its head. The radiating form has migrated from background lines to the head itself.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous works radiated lines from around the body; here the head is the radiating object — a spiked disc — while the body below remains sketchy and still, reversing the earlier relationship."}]},{"title":"Faces That Fill the Frame","introduction":"Four works expand the face until it crowds or consumes the available space, and the radiating marks become inseparable from the surface itself.","stops":[{"slot":"W027","whyHere":"Three nested circles stack on a red ground, the upper two with branching red lines radiating from blue centers, the lower opening into darkness. The face is now the entire composition, and the radiating marks are inside the eyes.","transitionFromPrevious":"W128's figure had a body beneath its radiant head; here the body disappears entirely and the radiating marks move inside the eye forms themselves, compressing the spread inward."},{"slot":"W074","whyHere":"Two paired eyes and a wide toothed mouth fill the frame edge to edge; the background radiates in dense layered stripes of orange, red, yellow, and green. No neutral space remains anywhere in the image.","transitionFromPrevious":"W027's face sat within a bordered red field; here the face and the radiating background merge so completely that figure and ground become the same dense, pressured surface."},{"slot":"W018","whyHere":"A masked form rises from dense scribbled lines, radiating blue-grey bands spreading behind it. The upper mask is smooth and legible; the lower body dissolves into the radiating marks, blurring the boundary between figure and field.","transitionFromPrevious":"W074's face was flat and frontal; W018 introduces depth and dissolution — the figure emerges from its own radiating marks rather than sitting in front of them."},{"slot":"W188","whyHere":"A blocky upright figure with concentric-ring eyes stands at center, radiating yellow-white lines bursting from behind its head into a crowded field of color blocks, scribbled loops, and a lone flower shape.","transitionFromPrevious":"W018's figure dissolved downward into marks; W188's figure holds its shape but the surrounding field is so dense with competing elements that the radiating lines behind the head are just one layer among many."}]},{"title":"When the Center Loosens","introduction":"Five works close the exhibition by complicating or dispersing the center — through layered spirals, curtained enclosures, and surfaces where the radiating mark and the ground become indistinguishable.","stops":[{"slot":"W104","whyHere":"placeholder — see reorder note; W104 already placed above","transitionFromPrevious":"placeholder"},{"slot":"W126","whyHere":"A large red-pink spiral dominates the upper left while stacked zigzag and wave bands fill the lower two-thirds. The center is off-axis and the radiating movement is lateral rather than outward from a figure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W188's radiating lines burst from behind a legible figure; W126 removes the figure entirely, leaving the spiral and the banded marks to compete without a body to anchor them."},{"slot":"W170","whyHere":"A large spiral coils from upper-center leftward, its dense core surrounded by horizontal banding, vertical bars, and scattered color patches. Two competing movements — inward spiral and outward bands — keep the surface unsettled.","transitionFromPrevious":"W126's spiral sat in one corner against flat bands; W170's spiral is larger and its core denser, so the tension between inward pull and outward spread feels more evenly matched."},{"slot":"W234","whyHere":"Dozens of red lines fall vertically from a wide banded canopy, enclosing a smaller looping form beneath. The radiating movement is downward and enclosing rather than outward, reversing the exhibition's dominant direction.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous spirals pulled inward; W234's lines fall downward and enclose, so the spread becomes a cage rather than an escape, introducing containment as a new possibility for the radiating mark."},{"slot":"W292","whyHere":"A gold form swells upward into a near-blinding bloom, then drops into hanging triangular points; the dark border is covered edge-to-edge in small looping and zigzag marks. The center is luminous but the surrounding scrawl presses back at equal intensity.","transitionFromPrevious":"W234's lines fell and enclosed; W292's central form rises and blooms, but the dense border scrawl surrounds it with the same insistence, so neither center nor edge dominates."},{"slot":"W011","whyHere":"A dark crowned form on an amber field, surrounded by competing spirals, hatch bands, looping lines, and scattered circles — no single radiating movement organizes the surface. The center is present but the marks refuse to settle around it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W292 held two temperatures in tension; W011 multiplies the competing marks until the radiating logic of the whole exhibition becomes hardest to locate, closing the journey in productive noise."},{"slot":"W167","whyHere":"Two glowing oval eyes inside a yellow-outlined mass, a hard white beam exiting to the right, the left edge compressed into white zigzags, the lower half open and scattered. The center is bright but asymmetric, and the radiating marks point in only one direction.","transitionFromPrevious":"W011's marks spread in every direction without resolution; W167 narrows the spread to a single hard beam, offering a last, directional answer to the exhibition's opening question before the journey ends."}]}]}
